Re-reviewed 2026-09-06 after ADR-116 excluded the two raw monthly readings retained in excluded_readings. The accepted 2015-onward series has 137 readings through 2026-07-31, with leading values 601,300, 600,100 and 599,900 acre-feet; the spike screen is clear. NID still gives Parker Dam (AZ10312) 180,000 acre-feet in every storage field, and the automatic admission still returns no dam close enough to confirm. Reclamation's Parker Dam page still publishes 646,200 acre-feet total at elevation 450 feet (https://www.usbr.gov/projects/index.php?id=207), but that is not a defensible current denominator: its newer allocation sheet supersedes earlier sheets and gives 590,262 total, 570,253 live and 176,837 active acre-feet (https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/Mohave-Havasu_ReservoirCapacityAllocations_2026.pdf). The current operations report uses 570,253 available acre-feet at 450 feet (https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/levels.html), while CDEC's reservoir profile still gives 648,000 without defining total versus live storage (https://cdec.water.ca.gov/dynamicapp/profile?s=HVS&type=res). Held for unresolved storage basis and survey transition: verify which volume and elevation-capacity table CDEC sensor 15 uses, when the new table reached its observations and whether earlier readings were recomputed, then establish matching dated full levels and a comparable 1991-2020 baseline. Passing the numerical screens at 646,200 does not settle those questions. No capacity is selected and no roster entry or normal is published. The two exclusions remain unchanged and provider issue https://github.com/buschbrian/western-water-dashboard/issues/44 remains open. See docs/operations/source-admission.md#lake-havasu-hvs-capacity-review.

Success Dam: Re-reviewed 2026-10-31. The June 2019 monthly reading of 91,530 acre-feet is real. It equals CDEC's daily value for 30 June 2019, and the daily peak was 92,775 acre-feet on 24 June. ADR-116 therefore does not apply. CDEC's reservoir report and profile give 82,300 acre-feet as full, the Corps' gross pool, and the reading is 11.2% above it. That is outside the 10% surcharge allowance, at the edge where ADR-065 refused Lake Mohave. USACE states that the spillway enlargement, complete in March 2025, raised total capacity to 112,000 acre-feet (https://www.dvidshub.net/news/500088/success-lake-capacity-increased-with-completion-critical-flood-risk-management-project, checked 2026-09-04). Under ADR-111 that is a later dated version and does not apply to 2019. CDEC still publishes 82,300. Research on 2026-09-04 found no citable Corps figure between 82,300 and the inventory's 230,000 that contains the 2019 water. An 84,095 figure appears only in unsourced summaries and is not used. Wikipedia, citing the 2006 CEQA notice for the seismic remediation, records a storage limit of 28,800 acre-feet from 2006. Readings above 80,000 in 2017 and 2019 show it was not in force then, and its end is not published. Held for a full level, not for a reading. Release needs a Corps full level for 2015 to 2025 that contains 92,775 acre-feet, with the date the enlarged pool came into use. A decision that revisits the allowance would also release it. Success Lake-Pool: Audited 2026-11-11 under SPK (ADR-155). Passes the screens on the inventory's 230,000 acre-feet, but California's withheld finding for the same water (SCC) holds it for a full level containing its 2019 water. A Corps series does not route around that hold (ADR-155). Schafer Dam / Success Lake: Audited 2026-11-11 under SPK (ADR-155). No storage series could be read. Tried: none.
